premise: I used my late husband’s $92,000 life insurance to buy a 50% stake in my stepson’s historic funeral home, signing a partnership contract, but after a $780,000 corporate buyout he forged a dissolution, sent me a $4,500 cremation check, and locked me out; I proved the forgery with bank records, voided the sale, and now run ‘Eulogy of Lies Memorials’ — my stepson digs graves by hand wearing a shirt that says ‘6 Feet Under Fraud,’ and every service program prints his perjury conviction number.
